title: A filtered colimit of algebras is the colimit of the underlying modules
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I$ a small filtered category and $i\mapsto A_i$ a functor from $I$ to the category of commutative $R$-algebras, with transition maps $A(u):A_i\to A_j$ for $u:i\to j$, colimit $A=\varinjlim_IA_i$ in that category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] and coprojections $\iota_i:A_i\to A$. Regard every $A_i$ and $A$ as $R$-modules and the $R$-algebra homomorphisms $A(u)$, $\iota_i$ as $R$-linear maps. Then $(A,(\iota_i)_{i\in I})$ is a colimit of the diagram $i\mapsto A_i$ in the category of $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]: for every $R$-module $P$ and $R$-linear maps $f_i:A_i\to P$ with $f_j\circ A(u)=f_i$ for all $u:i\to j$ there is exactly one $R$-linear map $f:A\to P$ with $f\circ\iota_i=f_i$ for all $i$.

source.place: not stated in Stacks for algebras; the module side is Algebra, Lemma Tag 00D6 (lemma-directed-colimit, line 778: elements of the colimit are classes of elements of the stages, sums and scalar multiples computed at a common later index), and the passage from the colimit of rings to the colimit of modules is used implicitly in Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07RI (lemma-colimit-etale, line 47654) and More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0AH1 (more-algebra-lemma-filtered-colimit-etale-noetherian-fibres); the directed-set case with base A_0 is written out in step 2 of lem-weil-pbc-directed-colimit-base-change-elementwise

proof.text: Step 1 (underlying ring and type colimits). Prove clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise] directly, including independent universes: equip each cocone of rings with the R-algebra structure induced by one stage; filteredness makes all stage structure maps agree at a common successor. Apply the algebra colimit universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] to obtain the unique ring map. Mathlib CommRingCat.FilteredColimits.forget_preservesFilteredColimits then gives an IsColimit of the underlying type cocone.

Step 2 (descent of the compatible functions). Regard the linear maps f_i as functions, and obtain their compatibility by taking underlying functions in the hypothesis hf. Apply Functor.CoconeTypes.IsColimit.desc to the type colimit from step 1; this gives g into the arbitrary-universe module P with g(ι_i(a)) = f_i(a). The type colimit universal property encapsulates well-definedness on representatives, without a separate ring equality criterion.

Step 3 (linearity). By the representability in [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise] and filteredness, Mathlib Types.FilteredColimit.jointly_surjective_of_isColimit₂ represents any two elements at one stage. Rewrite their sum using additivity of the coprojection, the identities of step 2, and additivity of f_i. For a scalar multiple, represent the element at one stage and use scalar compatibility of the coprojection and f_i. Package g as an R-linear map.

Step 4 (factorization and uniqueness). LinearMap.ext turns the identities of step 2 into equality of composites with every coprojection. Any other linear map with these composites agrees on every representative; every element is a representative by [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise]. Hence the descended map is unique.
